existing_mapping.evidence: The system offers a function for maintaining details such as unique number, name, address, and city for each parking lot.
The Administrator is connected to the system use case that allows updating parking lot details.
The same system use case that maintains parking lot details also handles the number of available spaces.
The Gate Sensor is intended to identify vehicle arrival and departure sending real-time data to the system.
Upon vehicle arrival, the system uses data from the gate sensor to search for the vehicle in the database.
If a vehicle is found, the gate sensor is instructed by the system to open the entrance barrier.
Instructions for client registration are followed if the vehicle is not recognized or if barriers do not open.
The registration process guides clients to enter personal and vehicle information including photos.
System processes photos during registration to automatically extract the details of the vehicle.
Vehicle colors are categorized into predefined groups during the photo extraction process.
Associations between clients and vehicles are updated to ensure each vehicle is linked to one client.
After updating records, the system commands the gate sensor to open the barrier.
The system records parking session information such as start time and vehicle details after the barrier passage.
Clients drive to conveyors, secure the vehicle, and leave it for system processing.
Conveyors' Controller scans vehicles, assigns conveyors, and optimizes parking space assignment.
Both parking space and conveyor locations are defined with specific floor and coordinate information.
Parking spaces have defined sizes to match vehicle accommodation needs.
Conveyors have maximum weights they can handle.
The optimization algorithm takes space size and weight capacity into account.
After parking is completed, the system is updated with the vehicle's final location.
The system consistently tracks vehicle locations on conveyors or in parking spaces.
Clients receive parking details via SMS as part of the session details feature.
Parking details are accessible through system UI if the client uses their phone number.
Conveyor handling information is necessary only during the parking session.
For vehicle retrieval, clients end parking through the system UI by entering relevant validation details.
On end parking request, a vacant conveyor is assigned to assist in vehicle retrieval to the gate.
Clients are prompted to complete payment via the system UI.
Payment rates are calculated annually based on IRS-provided price lists.
Each parking lot may apply different price structures as indicated in price list flexibilities.
The system maintains price history records for each parking lot.
The payment process is outsourced to an external Payment Gateway.
Once payment is confirmed through the Payment Gateway, the gate opens to allow vehicle exit.
Clients can request receipts from the system after payments are processed.
Receipts provide comprehensive transaction details once issued to the client.
Management of a client's club is included in the system's offered features.
Club members benefit from applicable discounts for parking sessions automatically.
Clients have the option to register for the club using the system UI.
Membership in the client's club is free and does not expire.
Clients can select their preferred parking lots and the preference data is auditable.
Members receive one free parking session in a selected lot during the first month after registration.
The system allows administrators to generate several types of reports including various company metrics.
Annual summary reports encompass revenue and demographic information for ParkWise.
Annual reports include details on payments and vehicle demographic data for each lot.
Annual reports are organized by city and total amounts in specified order.
Reports can be exported in PDF, and XML formats ensuring customizable outputs.
Reports tracking the club's growth are periodically generated.
Monthly club reports include member growth statistics and cumulative data explaining changes over time.
Club growth reports are arranged by month in chronological order.
